# Your report

We initialized the text-mining pipeline by loading the 20 Newsgroups corpus across four target categories (soc.religion.christian, sci.med, comp.graphics, and alt.atheism) using load_dataset_tool (result_id: load_dataset_1), yielding 2,257 total documents. Data hygiene was evaluated through check_missing_tool (result_id: check_missing_3) and check_duplicates_tool (result_id: check_duplicates_4), confirming zero missing values and zero duplicate entries. Next, describe_data_tool (result_id: describe_data_5) characterized document lengths across categories, revealing strong positive skewness with an overall mean length of 1,992.96 characters versus a median of 1,235 characters. Theological posts in soc.religion.christian exhibited the highest median length at 1,649 characters, whereas technical posts in comp.graphics had the shortest at 883 characters due to concise code snippets and queries.
![Document Length Distributions Across Categories](../plots/Hajer_Mastouri_agentic-pipeline_plot_describe_data_5.png)

Following initial inspection, the text collection was tokenized using tokenize_tool (result_id: tokenize_6) to produce 903,209 unigram tokens, averaging 400.18 tokens per document. We then transformed the tokens into a vector space representation using build_dtm_tool (result_id: dtm_7), applying boundary cutoffs alongside standard English stop-word filtering. This produced a Document-Term Matrix (DTM) of shape 2,257 * 8,583 containing 275,863 non-zero entries and an extreme sparsity rate of 98.576%. To visualize this sparse structure, dtm_heatmap_tool (result_id: dtm_heatmap_13) rendered a 20 * 20 positional submatrix, showing how alphabetical indexing placed header timestamp tokens ('00', '01', '081052') in the leading columns where counts were overwhelmingly zero aside from isolated low-frequency hits.
![Document-Term Matrix Heatmap](../plots/Hajer_Mastouri_agentic-pipeline_plot_dtm_heatmap_13.png)

To reduce the high dimensionality of the feature space, we executed variance_filter_tool across two trials. An initial threshold of 0.001 (result_id: variance_filter_9) removed zero terms because term frequencies easily exceeded fractional variances across 2,257 documents. Raising the threshold to 0.05 (result_id: variance_filter_10) pruned 7,002 near-constant terms (an 81.58% reduction), retaining the 1,581 most informative terms. Using this refined space, we investigated frequent co-occurrences via mine_patterns_tool (result_id: patterns_11) with the Top-K Fast Apriori (FAE) algorithm (k=10) under TF-IDF filtering for soc.religion.christian. The resulting top itemsets were entirely dominated by structural Usenet message headers—such as lines (support: 599), subject (support: 599), and organization (support: 536)—demonstrating that unstripped message headers persist across virtually 100% of forum posts even after stop-word removal.

We projected document vectors into a 2D space using Principal Component Analysis via reduce_dimensions_tool (result_id: reduction_12), capturing 29.88% total variance (20.51% PC1, 9.37% PC2). Most documents form a dense central cluster near the origin, with soc.religion.christian and alt.atheism sharing a negative trajectory along Component 2 due to overlapping philosophical and theological terms. In contrast, several comp.graphics postings appear as extreme outliers along Component 2. This confirms successful end-to-end execution of the pipeline, from raw data hygiene and sparse vector modeling to variance filtering, pattern discovery, and low-dimensional projection.

![PCA 2D Projection](../plots/Hajer_Mastouri_agentic-pipeline_plot_reduction_12.png)
